# Free Ad Attention Heatmap: See What People Notice First | AdSure
URL: https://www.adsure.in/heatmap
Summary: Free, no sign-up. Add your Meta or Google ad image or video and see where eyes land first, what gets skipped, and what to change. Your ad never leaves your device.

Free tool · No sign-up

## See where eyes land on your ad.

Add your ad image or video. In a few seconds you'll see what people notice first, how much attention your product and offer get, and what Instagram's buttons will cover, before you spend a rupee on it.

- Trained on real eye-tracking data
- Free, no sign-up
- Your ad never leaves your device

Choose your ad, or drop it here Image (JPG, PNG, WebP) or video (MP4, MOV) · up to 4 at once to compare versions

Reading your heatmap

### Four questions to ask about spots 1, 2 and 3.

If the first look goes to a background, a pattern or a logo, people scroll past before they know what you sell.

For sale and discount ads, the offer should sit in spot 1 or 2. Buried deals don't stop the scroll.

Faces win the first look. That's good if the person looks at, holds or uses the product. It's bad if they lead eyes away from it.

On Instagram and Facebook, captions, buttons and profile names cover the top and bottom. Keep key words away from the edges.

Be honest about what it is

### A heatmap shows attention. Not sales.

#### What it's good at

- Showing what stands out first and what gets lost
- Telling you whether your product and offer actually get seen
- Catching key words hidden under Reels and Stories buttons
- Comparing versions with one focus score out of 100

#### What it can't tell you

- Whether people will click, buy or fill a form
- Whether your offer or message makes sense to them
- Whether the ad breaks Meta, Google or Indian ad rules
- Whether your landing page or targeting will waste money

Be Sure with Adsure.

### Attention is step one. Will the ad actually sell?

AdSure's ad experts and AI review your creative, ad text, landing page and targeting, and tell you exactly what to fix before you spend. We never touch your ad account.

Questions

### Good to know

**Q: Is it really free?**
Yes. No sign-up, no limit on how many ads you check.

**Q: Is my ad uploaded anywhere?**
Not for the heatmap. The heatmap is worked out inside your browser. Your image or video never leaves your phone or computer, and AdSure never sees it. Close the tab and it's gone. The only exception is the optional free AI image. If you tap "Make my free AI image", a small copy of that one ad and our tips are sent to our AI to make it. Neither image is stored.

**Q: How does the free AI image work?**
After your heatmap, you can get one AI-improved version of an image ad, free and without signing up. It uses a basic AI model, so check the product and any text before you use it. To keep it fair, it's one per person. For more and sharper versions made from a full review by our experts and AI, join AdSure.

**Q: How does it predict where people look?**
It uses a model trained on real eye-tracking studies, where cameras recorded exactly where people looked at over a thousand images. The model learned what pulls the eye: faces, text, contrast and position. On slow connections we use a lighter, instant model instead, and the result says which one was used. It's a prediction, not a new eye-tracking study of your ad.

**Q: What does "Is your product seen?" do?**
Draw a box around your product, offer, logo or button. We show what share of attention each one gets and the order people see them in, so you know whether the thing you're paying to show actually gets noticed.

**Q: Does it work for video ads?**
Yes. It checks the opening frame, the one people see while they scroll, and one frame for each of the first 3 seconds, where most people decide to stay or scroll on.

**Q: Which ad sizes work?**
Any. Square (1:1), portrait (4:5), stories and reels (9:16) and landscape all work.

# Before you spend: a 12-point check for your Meta or Google ad | AdSure
URL: https://www.adsure.in/guides/ad-checklist
Summary: A simple 12-point check for Meta and Google ads in India: creative, ad text, landing page, tracking, budget, audience, timing and ad rules. Run it before you put money behind an ad.

Checklist

## Before you spend: a 12-point check for your ad

Most wasted ad money comes from a few common mistakes. Go through these 12 points before you put money behind an ad. It takes about 10 minutes.

By the AdSure ad team · Updated 24 November 2026 · 6 min read

### The creative

1. Show the product in the first second. On Reels and Stories most people decide in a moment whether to keep watching. If your product or brand only appears after a few seconds, many people never see it.
2. Keep text on the image short. A few words for the offer is enough. A busy image hides the product and is harder to read on a phone.
3. Use the right sizes. Square (1:1) or vertical (4:5) for feeds, and full-screen vertical (9:16) for Reels and Stories. A stretched or cropped creative looks careless.

### The ad text

1. One clear offer. Say what it is, what it costs or what someone gets, and why now. If a person can't repeat your offer after reading it once, it isn't clear yet.
2. No claims you can't prove. Words like "guaranteed", "100%", "best" or "No.1" need proof you can show. They can get the ad rejected and break Indian ad rules. Use real numbers instead, like "4.6 stars from 2,300 reviews". See our guide to Indian ad rules.
3. A button that matches the goal. "Shop now" for sales, "Sign up" or "Get quote" for leads, "Send message" for WhatsApp. A vague "Learn more" on a sales ad gets fewer buyers.

### The landing page

1. Same offer and price as the ad. If the ad says ₹899 and the page shows ₹1,199, people leave. The first thing they see after clicking should match what made them click.
2. Fast on a phone. Open the page on your own phone using mobile data. Google treats a page whose main content shows within 2.5 seconds as "good". Heavy images and too many apps are the usual reasons a page is slow.
3. Reasons to trust you. Reviews, a way to contact you (WhatsApp works well in India), a clear return or refund policy and a secure https link.

### Tracking, budget and audience

1. Tracking works before you spend. Make a test purchase or lead and check that Meta Events Manager or Google Ads records it. Without this, the platform can't learn who buys, and you can't tell which ad works.
2. Enough budget for each ad set. Meta says an ad set needs about 50 results in 7 days to leave the learning phase. A simple rule: daily budget per ad set ≈ your target cost per result × 50 ÷ 7. If that's too much, run fewer ad sets, usually just one, before you cut anything else.
3. Right audience and right time. Don't narrow the audience so much that it can't deliver. Exclude people who already bought. And plan around festivals and seasons: people start searching for festive products weeks before the day. See the 2027 festival ad calendar.

Want this done for you? AdSure checks all of this, and more, on your actual ad. Our AI scores it in under a minute, and our experts review the creative. See what we check.

### Sources

- Meta Business Help Centre: About the learning phase
- Google web.dev: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)

### More guides

- Indian ad rules in plain words
- Festival ad calendar 2027: when to start your ads

# Indian ad rules in plain words: ASCI, health claims, finance and gaming | AdSure
URL: https://www.adsure.in/guides/indian-ad-rules
Summary: The Indian ad rules that matter most for Meta and Google ads: ASCI's truthful-claims code, influencer labels, health and cure claims, loan ads under RBI rules, real-money gaming and fake urgency. Checked November 2026.

Ad rules

## Indian ad rules in plain words

Meta or Google approving your ad doesn't mean it's legal in India. These are the rules that catch small businesses most often, in plain words.

By the AdSure ad team · Updated 24 November 2026 · 7 min read

Last checked: November 2026. This is a simple summary to help you avoid common mistakes, not legal advice. For a specific case, ask a lawyer.

### 1. Claims must be true and provable (ASCI)

The Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) code says claims in ads must be truthful and backed by proof. In practice:

- Avoid "guaranteed", "100%", "best", "No.1", "permanent" or "instant results" unless you can show proof. Use specific facts, like "rated 4.6 by 2,300 buyers".
- A disclaimer can explain a claim, but it can't contradict it or hide important conditions. "Free*" with a big condition in small print is not OK.
- If you say "free", say the condition next to it, for example "Free gift on orders above ₹999".

### 2. Influencer and creator ads need a clear label

- If a creator got money, free products or anything else from you, the post must say so upfront with a label like "Ad", "Sponsored", "Collaboration", "Partnership" or "Free gift". Not hidden among hashtags.
- In videos the label must stay on screen long enough to read. ASCI asks for at least 3 seconds on videos up to 15 seconds, and a third of the video for videos of 15 seconds to 2 minutes.
- Creators giving health or nutrition advice should have the right qualifications, and stock market advice needs SEBI registration.
- Under the Consumer Protection Act, the CCPA can fine misleading ads and can stop endorsers from endorsing for a period.

### 3. Health ads: never claim to cure a listed disease

The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 bans ads that claim a product can cure, treat or prevent the diseases listed in it. The list includes diabetes, obesity, cancer, heart disease and blood pressure. It also covers claims about sexual capacity and menstrual problems. Penalties include jail.

- Use careful words like "supports" or "helps manage", backed by evidence. Never use "cures" or "permanent results".
- On Meta, health, weight loss and weight gain ads should only be shown to people aged 18 and over.

### 4. Loans and finance ads (RBI and platform checks)

- Under RBI's Digital Lending Directions, loan offers must name the regulated lender, such as the bank or NBFC, and show the key facts, including the annual percentage rate (APR).
- Don't present an RBI listing as RBI approval or endorsement, and don't use pressure tricks.
- Google requires financial services advertisers in India to be verified before ads can run. Meta has its own checks for finance and stock advice.

### 5. Real-money gaming ads are banned

The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 bans offering and advertising online money games, like fantasy sports for cash, rummy or poker for money, and betting. It has been in force since 1 May 2026. Advertising can mean up to 2 years in jail and a fine of up to ₹50 lakh. Gaming companies have challenged the law in the Supreme Court, but the court has not paused it, so the ban applies. Google also stopped rummy and daily fantasy sports ads in India from January 2026.

### 6. No fake urgency or tricks

- "Only 2 left!" or "Offer ends tonight" must be true. India's dark pattern guidelines (2023) and ASCI's rules on deceptive design ban false urgency and similar tricks.
- Don't make ads look like news stories or use a news outlet's name or logo to sell.
- Crypto and NFT ads need ASCI's risk disclaimer.

Not sure about your ad? AdSure checks your ad text against these rules before you publish, and flags anything risky with a safer way to say it. See what we check.

### Sources

- ASCI: The ASCI Code
- ASCI: Code guidelines (influencers, disclaimers, deceptive design and more)
- India Code: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
- PRS: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025
- Google Ads: Update to Gambling and Games policy (India)
- Meta: Unacceptable business practices

# Festival ad calendar 2027 for India: when to start your ads | AdSure
URL: https://www.adsure.in/guides/festival-ad-calendar-2027
Summary: Every big Indian festival and sale date in 2027, from Holi (22 March) to Diwali (29 October), with a suggested date to start your ads and what people buy.

Calendar

## Festival ad calendar 2027: when to start your ads

People start searching for festive products weeks before the day. If your ads start on the day itself, you've missed most of the season. Here are the 2027 dates and when to start.

By the AdSure ad team · Updated 24 November 2026 · 4 min read

### 2027 dates and when to start

"Start ads by" is three weeks before each date. That's a good starting point for most products. Gifts and big purchases often need longer, and some products peak much earlier.

| Festival | Date | Start ads by | What people buy |
| Makar Sankranti / Pongal | Fri, 15 Jan 2027 | 25 Dec 2026 | Kites, sweets, regional food, home |
| Republic Day sales | Tue, 26 Jan 2027 | 5 Jan 2027 | Electronics, fashion, home |
| Valentine's Day | Sun, 14 Feb 2027 | 24 Jan 2027 | Gifts, flowers, jewellery, restaurants |
| Eid al-Fitr* | Wed, 10 Mar 2027 | 17 Feb 2027 | Fashion, sweets, gifts, food |
| Holi | Mon, 22 Mar 2027 | 1 Mar 2027 | Colours, sweets, white clothing, travel |
| Independence Day | Sun, 15 Aug 2027 | 25 Jul 2027 | Sales, tricolour products, travel |
| Raksha Bandhan | Tue, 17 Aug 2027 | 27 Jul 2027 | Rakhis, gifts, sweets, hampers |
| Janmashtami | Wed, 25 Aug 2027 | 4 Aug 2027 | Puja items, kids' costumes, sweets |
| Ganesh Chaturthi | Sat, 4 Sep 2027 | 14 Aug 2027 | Idols, decor, modaks, puja items |
| Onam | Sun, 12 Sep 2027 | 22 Aug 2027 | Kerala fashion, sadya, home |
| Navratri begins | Thu, 30 Sep 2027 | 9 Sep 2027 | Chaniya choli, ethnic wear, jewellery |
| Dussehra | Sat, 9 Oct 2027 | 18 Sep 2027 | Vehicles, electronics, gold, home |
| Karva Chauth | Mon, 18 Oct 2027 | 27 Sep 2027 | Jewellery, beauty, ethnic wear |
| Dhanteras | Wed, 27 Oct 2027 | 6 Oct 2027 | Gold, silver, utensils, electronics |
| Diwali | Fri, 29 Oct 2027 | 8 Oct 2027 | Sweets, gifts, decor, fashion, home, everything |
| Christmas | Sat, 25 Dec 2027 | 4 Dec 2027 | Cakes, gifts, decor, party wear |

*Eid depends on the moon and can move by a day. Some festivals, like Raksha Bandhan, Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi and Navratri, fall a day apart in different regional calendars. Republic Day is a date when many online sales run, not a festival. Check your local calendar before you plan big spends.

### How to plan around a festival

1. Start early, with a small budget. Launch two to three weeks before. This gives Meta and Google time to learn who buys, before costs go up.
2. Raise the budget when searches rise. Interest usually climbs steadily in the last 1 to 2 weeks. Spend more when people are actively looking, not before.
3. Expect higher costs at peak. In the days before Diwali many brands compete for the same people, so each click or sale can cost more. Have your best creative and offer ready before then.
4. Stop or lower spend after the day. Interest drops quickly once a festival has passed. Check delivery dates: an order that can't arrive in time is a refund waiting to happen.
5. Plan creatives in advance. Make festive versions of your best ads early, and check them before the rush. Ads can take time to get approved.

Your product's own timing. Every product peaks differently. AdSure looks at 5 years of Google searches in India for what you sell and shows when your searches start rising, when to raise your budget and which states search most. For example, searches for kaju katli jump about 7 times around Diwali and start rising about 3 weeks before. See the timing tool.

- Drik Panchang: Indian calendar 2027

# Privacy Policy | AdSure
URL: https://www.adsure.in/privacy
Summary: How AdSure collects, uses and protects your personal data, who we share it with, and your rights under India's data protection law.

Legal

## Privacy Policy

Last updated: 16 October 2026

- We collect what you give us (like your contact details and your ads) and basic usage data.
- We use it to review your ads, contact you and run AdSure. We never sell it.
- Payments go through Razorpay. We never see your full card, UPI or bank details.
- You can ask us to see, correct or delete your data anytime at hi@adsure.in.

### Who we are

AdSure ("AdSure", "we", "us") is a company made in India. We run www.adsure.in and app.adsure.in. This policy explains what personal data we collect, why, who we share it with, and the choices and rights you have, including under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

### What we collect

#### When you join early access

Your name, phone number, email, type of business, monthly ad spend range, where you run ads, and your biggest problem (if you tell us).

#### When you use AdSure

- Your account details, like your name and email.
- What you share for a review: ad images and videos, ad text, landing page links, targeting and budget details, your industry and the competitors you choose.
- Questions you ask in Ask an expert. If you speak, we turn your voice into text to answer you.
- Notes from expert calls you book.

#### When you use the AdSure browser extension

The AdSure extension for Chrome works only on Meta Ads Manager, and only when you click Add this page. It reads what Ads Manager shows you on that screen: campaign, ad set and ad names, their results and costs (like amount spent, results, reach, impressions, clicks and return on ad spend), delivery status, budgets, any breakdown you have turned on (like age, gender or placement), the date range, your ad account number, and, if you have it open, the settings of an ad set or ad (like its goal, audience, placements, ad text and link). It also takes a small preview picture of each ad.

Until you press Send to AdSure, this stays in the extension on your computer. When you send it, it is saved to your AdSure account so we can make your report, and the extension deletes its copy. The extension only reads: it never clicks, types or changes anything in your ad account, and it never reads your password, payment details or messages. We use this data only to give you your reports and advice, and to improve AdSure's checks. We never sell it or use it for advertising.

#### When you pay

Payments are handled by Razorpay. We don't see or store your full card, UPI or bank details. We get a payment ID and whether the payment worked.

#### When you visit our website or app

Basic technical data like your device, browser, IP address and the pages you visit. We use Microsoft Clarity to see how people use our pages (with heatmaps and session recordings). Form fields like your name, email and phone are hidden from these recordings. We use Cloudflare Turnstile to check that forms are filled by a real person.

#### When you use the free AI image on our heatmap page

The heatmap runs only in your browser. If you choose the free AI image, a small copy of that one ad and our tips are sent to our AI provider (Cloudflare Workers AI) to make it. We don't store your ad or the new image. To keep it to one free image per person, we save a scrambled code (a hash) made from your IP address and a random ID kept in your browser, never the address itself. We delete these within 90 days.

#### Public information

To research your market, we look at public information about other businesses, like ads in public ad libraries, Google search trends and public web pages, including your own landing page.

### How we use it

- To run AdSure: review your ads, build your reports and score, answer your questions, run competitor research and checks, and let our experts help you.
- To contact you about early access, your seat, your account and your reviews, by email, phone or WhatsApp, as you agreed when you signed up.
- To take payments, prevent fraud and keep AdSure secure.
- To improve AdSure and train our AI, using ads you share with your name, contact details and business identity removed. You can ask us to stop at any time.
- To follow the law, such as tax and accounting rules.

We will never sell your personal data, and we never publish your ads or show them to other customers.

### Who we share it with

We share only what each one needs to do its job:

| Who | Why |
| Our ad experts | To review your ads and run your expert calls |
| Supabase | Stores our database and your files |
| Vercel | Hosts our website and app |
| Razorpay | Takes payments |
| Resend | Sends our emails, like login links and reminders |
| AI model providers | Analyse your ads and answer your questions |
| Microsoft Clarity and Cloudflare | Show us how pages are used, and stop bots |
| Google and Apify | Fetch public data like search trends, page speed and public ads. We send search words and links, not your personal details. |

We may also share data if the law requires it, to protect people's safety, or if AdSure is merged or sold (in which case this policy still protects your data).

### Where your data is stored

Some of our service providers store or process data on servers outside India. When that happens, we use providers with strong security, and we follow Indian law on sending data abroad.

### How long we keep it

- Early access details: until you ask us to delete them, or until we no longer need them to contact you about AdSure.
- Ad reports from the browser extension or an Ads Manager file: while your account is open, or until you delete the report in the app.
- Account data and your ads: while your account is open. After you close it, we delete or anonymise it within 120 days, unless the law asks us to keep some of it.
- Payment and invoice records: as long as Indian tax and accounting laws require.

### Your rights

You can ask us to:

- tell you what personal data we have about you and how we use it;
- correct, complete or update it;
- delete it;
- stop contacting you, or withdraw your consent at any time (this doesn't affect what we did before);
- stop using your ads to improve AdSure;
- let someone else use these rights for you if you die or can't act yourself (nomination).

Write to hi@adsure.in from the email you used with us. We will reply as soon as we can, and within the time the law requires. If you're not happy with our answer, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.

### Cookies and browser storage

Our website uses a small amount of browser storage to remember things like whether you've already joined or closed the sign-up popup. Microsoft Clarity and Cloudflare Turnstile may set cookies to do their jobs. You can block or clear cookies in your browser settings. The site will still work, though some parts may not remember your choices.

### How we protect it

All data travels over a secure connection (https). Access to customer data is limited to the people who need it, and our team's admin tools need two-step login. No system is perfectly secure, but if a breach ever affects your data, we will tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

### Children

AdSure is for businesses and adults. We don't knowingly collect data from anyone under 18. If you think a child has given us their details, write to us and we will delete them.

### Grievance Officer

If you have a question or complaint about your personal data, contact our Grievance Officer:
